LESSON: READING 8.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: POEM

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.2: Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading: Poem

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading: Poem. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: when giving an opinion. 1. How can one tell the meaning of unfamiliar words used in a text?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use non-verbal cues to bring out the message in a poem

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: READING 8.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: POEM
This lesson teaches Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading: Poem for Grade 8 ENGLISH.

STUDY STEPS
1. use non-verbal cues to bring out the message in a poem
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading: Poem using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading: Poem above.
2. Explain Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading: Poem to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading: Poem.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading: Poem with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading: Poem important for a Grade 8 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. when giving an opinion. 1. How can one tell the meaning of unfamiliar words used in a text?
2. Why should one support an opinion about a story or person with evidence?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. use non-verbal cues to bring out the message in a poem

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
